title: 327. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Exterior Angle Theorem for Triangles
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the relationship between an exterior angle of a triangle and its remote interior angles.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the Exterior Angle Theorem for a triangle?

options.label: A
options.text: An exterior angle equals its adjacent interior angle.

options.label: B
options.text: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

questions.explanation: The Exterior Angle Theorem states that the measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of the two remote interior angles. Option A is incorrect because an exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle are supplementary and need not be equal. Therefore, the correct statement is option B.
questions.hint: Recall that remote interior angles are the two interior angles not adjacent to the exterior angle.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate an exterior angle using the two remote interior angles.
questions.question: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles for an exterior angle measure \(40^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\). What is the measure of the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Therefore, the exterior angle measures \(40^\circ + 60^\circ = 100^\circ\). Hence, the correct measure is \(100^\circ\).
questions.hint: Add the measures of the two remote interior angles.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a remote interior angle given the exterior angle and the other remote interior angle.
questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle measures \(120^\circ\). One remote interior angle measures \(45^\circ\). What is the measure of the other remote interior angle?
questions.explanation: The Exterior Angle Theorem gives that the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Therefore, the other remote interior angle is \(120^\circ - 45^\circ = 75^\circ\). Thus, the correct measure is \(75^\circ\).
questions.hint: Subtract the known remote interior angle from the exterior angle.

questions.learningObjective: Use the supplementary relationship to find the adjacent interior angle of a given exterior angle.
questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle measures \(130^\circ\). What is the measure of its adjacent interior angle?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight angle, so they are supplementary. Therefore, the adjacent interior angle measures \(180^\circ - 130^\circ = 50^\circ\). Hence, the correct measure is \(50^\circ\).
questions.hint: Use the fact that an exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle add to \(180^\circ\).

questions.concept: Exterior Angle with One Unknown Remote Interior Angle
questions.learningObjective: Solve for a missing remote interior angle using the Exterior Angle Theorem.
questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle measures \(110^\circ\). One remote interior angle measures \(50^\circ\). What is the measure of the other remote interior angle?
questions.explanation: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Therefore, the other remote interior angle is \(110^\circ - 50^\circ = 60^\circ\). Thus, the correct measure is \(60^\circ\).
questions.hint: Set the exterior angle equal to the sum of the two remote interior angles.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an algebraic equation using the Exterior Angle Theorem.
questions.question: In a triangle, an exterior angle measures \(3x+10\). The two remote interior angles measure \(x+20\) and \(x+30\). What is the measure of the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, \(3x+10 = (x+20) + (x+30)\). Combining the right side gives \(3x+10 = 2x+50\). Subtracting \(2x\) from both sides gives \(x+10 = 50\), so \(x = 40\). The exterior angle is \(3(40)+10 = 130^\circ\). Therefore, the correct measure is \(130^\circ\).
questions.hint: Set the exterior angle equal to the sum of the two remote interior angle expressions.

questions.learningObjective: Identify an inequality relationship involving an exterior angle and its remote interior angles.
questions.question: Which statement is always true for an exterior angle of a triangle?

options.label: A
options.text: It is greater than each of its remote interior angles.

options.label: B
options.text: It is equal to its adjacent interior angle.

questions.explanation: The Exterior Angle Theorem implies that an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Since both remote interior angles have positive measure, the exterior angle must be greater than each one individually. Option B is false because an exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle are supplementary and are not always equal. Therefore, the correct statement is option A.
questions.hint: Compare the exterior angle with each remote interior angle, remembering that both remote interior angles are positive.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a missing exterior angle using the sum of exterior angles of a triangle.
questions.question: In a triangle, two exterior angles measure \(110^\circ\) and \(130^\circ\). What is the measure of the third exterior angle?
questions.explanation: The sum of the exterior angles of a triangle, one at each vertex, is \(360^\circ\). Therefore, the third exterior angle is \(360^\circ - (110^\circ + 130^\circ) = 360^\circ - 240^\circ = 120^\circ\). Thus, the correct measure is \(120^\circ\).
questions.hint: Recall that the exterior angles of a triangle, one at each vertex, add to \(360^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve a multi-step equation using the Exterior Angle Theorem.
questions.question: In a triangle, an exterior angle measures \(5x\). The two remote interior angles measure \(2x+20\) and \(x+40\). What is the measure of the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, \(5x = (2x+20) + (x+40)\). Combining the right side gives \(5x = 3x+60\). Subtracting \(3x\) from both sides gives \(2x = 60\), so \(x = 30\). The exterior angle is \(5(30) = 150^\circ\). Therefore, the correct measure is \(150^\circ\).
questions.hint: First write an equation from the Exterior Angle Theorem, then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Exterior Angle and Adjacent Interior Angle Synthesis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the adjacent interior angle after solving for an exterior angle.
questions.question: In a triangle, an exterior angle at \(A\) measures \(4x+10\). The two remote interior angles measure \(x+30\) and \(2x-10\). What is the measure of the interior angle at \(A\)?
questions.explanation: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, \(4x+10 = (x+30) + (2x-10)\). Combining the right side gives \(4x+10 = 3x+20\). Subtracting \(3x\) from both sides gives \(x+10 = 20\), so \(x = 10\). The exterior angle is \(4(10)+10 = 50^\circ\). The interior angle at \(A\) is supplementary to this exterior angle, so it measures \(180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ\). Therefore, the correct measure is \(130^\circ\).
questions.hint: Find the exterior angle first, then use the supplementary relationship to find the adjacent interior angle.
